label.title: MCP Server — Operation Access Control
label.description: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) server lets AI assistants run Jahia GraphQL operations through the tool community.graphql.execute. Choose here which operations it may run. Queries and mutations are allowed separately: allowing a query never allows the mutation of the same name. Schema introspection (__schema, __type, __typename) is always allowed.
label.helpEntries: Each checked item adds one entry to the allow list: query:<path> or mutation:<path>, where <path> is a field name followed by sub-field names separated by dots, for example query:jcr.nodeByPath. Checking an item allows it and everything under it.
label.helpDefault: While the allow list is empty, the read-only default applies: every query except the admin namespace is allowed, and every mutation is refused. Queries under admin (query:admin…) must be listed explicitly. As soon as the list has one entry, only the listed operations are allowed. Mutations always need an explicit entry. Some mutations can never be allowed: communityMcp, which changes these settings, admin.jahia.configuration, which changes Jahia's OSGi configuration, and the operations that grant privileges: admin.personalApiTokens and any grantRoles or revokeRoles field.
label.helpAllowAll: “Allow all queries” checks every query that exists today except the admin namespace, which exposes configuration values: check admin yourself if it is needed. “Allow all mutations” checks every mutation that exists today, except those that can never be allowed. Operations added later, for example by a Jahia upgrade or a new module, are not included.
label.helpKeyboard: Keyboard: Tab moves into each list. Up and Down arrows move between items, Right arrow expands an item or moves to its first field, Left arrow collapses it or moves to its parent, Home and End go to the first and last item, Space or Enter checks or unchecks the item.
label.policyReadOnly: The allow list is empty, so the read-only default applies: every query except the admin namespace is allowed, and every mutation is refused.
label.policyRestricted: Only the checked operations are allowed. Every other query and mutation is refused.
label.policyNoQuery: No query is checked: every query will be refused. Only the checked mutations are allowed.
label.policyDenyAll: The allow list only holds entries the server ignores or always refuses, so every query and every mutation is refused. Removing them all restores the read-only default.
label.migrated: Some saved entries used the old format and were converted to “query:” entries. Save to keep the new format.
label.problemEntriesHint: These entries are in the allow list but are not shown in the lists below. Entries refused or ignored by the server must be removed before you can save. Remove the others unless you expect them to come back.
label.problemUnknown: Not found in the current GraphQL schema.
label.problemInvalid: Ignored by the server: not a valid query: or mutation: entry. Remove it before saving.
label.problemLocked: Always refused by the server: the allow list cannot open its own settings. Remove it before saving.
label.problemLockedConfiguration: Always refused by the server: the allow list cannot open changes to Jahia's OSGi configuration. Remove it before saving.
label.problemLockedPrivilege: Always refused by the server: the allow list cannot open operations that grant privileges (roles, personal API tokens). Remove it before saving.
label.filterHint: Matches the names and paths of operations and of fields already expanded.
label.queriesNoteDefault: Every query except the admin namespace is allowed while the allow list is empty. Check queries to allow only those.
label.queriesNoteRestricted: Only the checked queries are allowed.
label.mutationsNote: Only the checked mutations are allowed. Mutations change content and permissions: allow only what you need.
label.confirmClearBody: This change leaves the allow list empty, which restores the read-only default: every query except the admin namespace will be allowed, and every mutation refused. Nothing changes on the server until you save.
label.confirmClearQueriesBody: Mutations stay checked, so the allow list will not be empty: every query will be refused. Nothing changes on the server until you save.
label.confirmAllowMutationsBody: AI assistants will be able to run every mutation that exists today, including deleting and publishing content and changing permissions. Nothing changes on the server until you save.
label.confirmAllowAdminBody: The admin query namespace exposes Jahia's configuration values, including secrets such as passwords and keys. AI assistants will be able to read them. Allow it only if they really need it. Nothing changes on the server until you save.
label.coveredBy: Allowed because “{{parent}}” is checked. Uncheck “{{parent}}” to choose individual fields.
label.lockedNode: Cannot be allowed: the server always refuses changes to the MCP settings through the MCP server.
label.lockedConfigurationNode: Cannot be allowed: the server always refuses changes to Jahia's OSGi configuration through the MCP server.
label.lockedPrivilegeNode: Cannot be allowed: the server always refuses operations that grant privileges (roles, personal API tokens) through the MCP server.
label.adminQueryNode: Exposes configuration values, including secrets. Not allowed by the read-only default. Checking it asks for confirmation.
label.loadFieldsError: Could not load the fields of {{name}}. Expand it again to retry.
label.allEntriesSummary: Show all entries in the allow list ({{count}})
label.serverChanged: The allow list saved on the server changed while you were editing. Your changes are kept: “Discard changes” restores the list the server holds now.
label.saveSuccessCluster: Settings saved on this node only. Jahia runs in a cluster and the allow list is not replicated: save the same list on every other node, or set it through provisioning.
label.clusterNote: Jahia runs in a cluster. The allow list is stored on each node separately: saving here changes this node only. Set the same list on every node, by opening this page on each of them or through provisioning, or AI assistants get a different policy depending on the node that serves them.
label.saveError: The settings were not saved. Check the entries and try again.
label.saveBlocked: The settings were not saved. The server refuses these entries: {{entries}}. Remove them under “Entries that need your attention”, then save again.
label.saveErrorServer: The settings were not saved. The server said:
label.saveNetworkError: Could not reach the server. Check your connection and try again.
label.loadError: The MCP settings could not be loaded. Nothing has been changed. Try again, or reload the page.
label.schemaLoadError: The GraphQL operations could not be loaded, so the allow list cannot be edited. Try again, or reload the page.
